$comment: Enum values in this file are illustrative subsets of Biolink. At runtime compile_schema.py replaces every Biolink-derived enum with the complete set from the loaded biolink-model.yaml. See src/planner_agent/compile_schema.py.
title: BiomedicalQueryPlan
description: A standalone, structured Biolink query recommendation produced from a natural-language biomedical question. It may be used directly by a human, submitted to a compatible query system, or consumed by an Executor Agent. v0.10.0 requires explicit, complete candidate-explanation fan-out and documents inline directional-signature planning.

plan_version.description: Semver of THIS plan schema. Bump on breaking changes.

biolink_version.description: Semver of the Biolink Model release the predicates/categories in this plan were drawn from.

question.description: The verbatim natural-language question from the user.

plan_mode.description: Overall plan mode. `discovery` = variable-endpoint template paths (find candidates). `explanation` = two specific endpoints, use the path-between tool to explain their connection. `hybrid` = combine predicate-based discovery with explanation queries that either explain discovered candidates or provide independent fixed-endpoint context/fallback.

interpretation.description: The planner's parsed reading of the question.

archetypes.description: Which drug-repurposing question archetype(s) this maps to. Multi-label allowed for hybrid questions.

restated_question.description: The planner's own one-sentence restatement of the question. Used for debugging and eval.

intent.description: Linguistic signal for mode selection. `discovery` triggers on 'which/what/any/find'. `validation` triggers on 'why/how/does/is/explain'.

assumptions.description: Assumptions the planner made when the question was underspecified.

entities.description: Named entities extracted from the question. Names are surface strings; the chosen query system resolves them to CURIEs. Every entity_ref used in paths or explanation queries MUST appear here.

paths.description: Discovery-mode paths. Required when plan_mode is `discovery` or `hybrid`. Ordered list; order = ranking priority. Omit or leave empty in pure `explanation` mode.

explanation_queries.description: Explanation-mode queries. Required when plan_mode is `explanation` or `hybrid`. Each item is a call to the two-endpoint path-between tool. In hybrid mode an item may explain discovered candidates or independently assess fixed-endpoint context without gating candidate discovery. Omit or leave empty in pure `discovery` mode.

ranking.description: Explicit, stage-specific ranking instructions. `candidate_ranking` ranks discovered entities; `explanation_ranking` ranks paths returned across explanation queries. Query-local ExplanationReturn still controls paths within one explanation query.

evidence_policy.description: Hard evidence filters explicitly requested by the user. Planner recommendations belong in ranking criteria or evidence_recommendations instead.

evidence_recommendations.description: Portable, non-filtering evidence metadata that the user or planner recommends reporting with results. These recommendations remain useful without the project Executor.

aggregation.description: How results across paths / explanation queries should be combined into a final candidate list.

confidence.description: Planner's categorical self-assessment, anchored to structural properties of THIS plan (not a subjective introspective score). Level is derived by checking anchor conditions in `reasons`.

level.description: Anchored bins: `high` = all entities extracted with unambiguous names, question maps cleanly to a single archetype, all paths use predicates the planner recognizes, no gaps flagged. `medium` = at least one of: multiple archetypes, one gap flagged with a viable workaround, up to two stated assumptions, or moderate name ambiguity that is documented. `low` = multiple assumptions, ambiguous entity names, gaps that materially degrade the plan, or path templates the planner is uncertain about. If conditions for `low` are exceeded (e.g., cannot ground an entity name, cannot map to any archetype, cannot produce any valid path), the planner MUST NOT emit a plan and MUST return `refusal` with reason `needs_clarification` or `insufficient_information`.

reasons.description: Structural anchors that justify `level`. Every emitted plan must list at least one reason. Examples: 'single_archetype', 'no_gaps_flagged', 'all_entities_unambiguous', 'one_gap_workaround', 'multiple_assumptions', 'ambiguous_entity_name'. This is the field that eval and downstream gating should actually consume; `level` is a summary of it.

gaps.description: Biolink or KG modeling gaps the planner detected. Populated when the question cannot be fully expressed with in-model predicates or with the available tools.

refusal.description: If set, the planner declines to produce an executable plan. The semantic contract requires entities=[] and omission of paths, explanation_queries, ranking, aggregation, and evidence_policy. Use reason `needs_clarification` when the question is underspecified (no human-in-the-loop is available; the planner cannot ask follow-up questions).

notes.description: Free-form planner notes for a user, query system, or executor.

allOf.description: In discovery mode WITHOUT a refusal, at least one Path is required.
In explanation mode WITHOUT a refusal, at least one ExplanationQuery is required and paths must be empty or absent.
In hybrid mode WITHOUT a refusal, both paths and explanation_queries must be non-empty.

entity_ref.description: Local reference used inside paths and explanation queries (e.g. 'e1', 'disease_x'). Must be unique within this plan.

name.description: Surface name as it appeared (or was normalized in-question) in the user's text. The chosen query system resolves it unless input_binding supplies identifiers or an external input.

aliases.description: Optional alternative surface names a resolver may try if the primary name fails to resolve.

biolink_category.description: The Biolink category class the entity is expected to belong to.

is_variable.description: Required binding state. True means a discovery placeholder such as 'any Drug'; false means a fixed name, identifier set, or external input. Path.return_entity_ref defines the contextual target, and explanation endpoint bindings define contextual endpoints, so entities do not carry a global role.

taxa.description: Taxa allowed when grounding or binding this entity. Use NCBITaxon CURIEs; for example, NCBITaxon:9606 for human. This constrains entity identity, not the species context of evidence edges.

input_binding.description: Optional non-resolver binding for identifiers supplied by the user or an upstream workflow. The planner must never invent these identifiers or input references.

constraints.description: Optional constraints the chosen query system should apply to this entity after resolution.

query_role.description: Whether this entity is part of the query or only names context. 'queried' (the default) means some hop, explanation query or binding must reference it; a fixed entity nothing references is a plan that silently dropped part of the question. 'context' is a deliberate declaration that the entity is named for provenance or interpretation and is not queried — as in Q3_signature_reversal, where the disease names the source of the expression signature while the query runs over genes. Marking an entity 'context' requires `notes` saying why, because the whole point is that the omission was a choice rather than an oversight.

EntityInputBinding.description: A pre-resolved identifier set or a reference to a typed external input supplied at execution time.

identifiers.description: One or more CURIEs explicitly supplied by the user or upstream workflow.

input_ref.description: Stable name of an input supplied to the chosen query system by an upstream workflow.

direction_filter.description: For a directional_gene_signature, select input rows by their source signature direction. This is the disease/state direction, not the desired drug effect. Signature-reversal paths use the opposite direction on the drug's expression edge.

EntityConstraint.description: The planner's only supported hard entity constraint. `approval_status` is plan-level, portable semantic vocabulary rather than a Biolink slot or backend attribute: `approved` means currently marketed for any indication, while `ever_approved` also includes discontinued or withdrawn drugs. A query system may translate these values to its own attributes but must report the translation and must not silently relax the filter.

field.description: Portable semantic field supported by this plan contract.

op.description: Approval is an eligibility requirement, so only exact semantic matching is supported.

value.description: Use `approved` for currently marketed drugs; use `ever_approved` only when the user explicitly includes previously approved, discontinued, or withdrawn drugs.

Path.description: A discovery-mode path template built from Biolink predicates. return_entity_ref is the contextual target and must be variable. Every enabled path must also contain at least one non-variable entity as a fixed query anchor.

return_entity_ref.description: Contextual target returned by this path. In discovery and hybrid plans it must reference an entity with is_variable=true.

expected_result_category.description: Optional category from the loaded Biolink Model expected for returned candidates. The category of return_entity_ref must be this category or one of its Biolink descendants.

Hop.description: One directed Biolink edge. subject_ref and object_ref must identify different entities; self-loop hops are unsupported. Semantic validation also restricts qualifier-bearing hops to the regulates, affects, and interacts_with predicate families and their active descendants in the loaded Biolink Model.

predicate.description: Active, non-deprecated Biolink predicate slot name (e.g., 'biolink:treats'). Semantic validation checks it against the loaded model.

ExplanationQuery.description: A call to the two-endpoint path-between tool. The two endpoint bindings must identify different entities and must not share a discovery source; self-loop explanation queries are unsupported. The tool takes two resolved specific entities and returns all paths between them up to length k. It supports middle-node category constraints only. Predicate/qualifier/evidence constraints must be applied as post-filters on the returned paths. When this query is the required fallback for a predicate hop between two fixed entities, do not set predicate_whitelist or required_predicates_anywhere; the fallback must remain able to reveal alternative KG-supported connections.

rationale.description: One-sentence explanation of why this two-endpoint query answers (part of) the question.

max_hops.description: Upper bound k on path length passed to the tool. Keep small (2-4) to control combinatorial blowup, especially when middle categories are not tightly constrained.

middle_category_whitelist.description: Categories from the loaded Biolink Model allowed for intermediate nodes. Multiple categories = union. Omit to allow any category (not recommended at k>=3).

middle_category_blacklist.description: Categories from the loaded Biolink Model forbidden for intermediate nodes (applied after whitelist).

post_filter.description: Post-processing filters the chosen query system applies to returned paths. This is where predicate/qualifier/evidence constraints live when the path-finding tool does not enforce them at query time.

return.description: How many returned paths to keep, and how to rank them.

EndpointBinding.description: How one contextual explanation endpoint is bound. Its position as endpoint_a or endpoint_b defines its role for that query. Bind either directly to a non-variable Entity, or dynamically to aggregated discovery returns that are resolved before each hybrid explanation query executes.

entity_ref.description: Reference to an Entity in `entities`. That entity MUST have is_variable=false, because the tool requires resolved specific endpoints.

from_path_ids.description: Non-empty list of enabled discovery `path_id` values. Each Path supplies its own `return_entity_ref`; those candidate sets are combined using the plan's `aggregation`, deduplicated, and ranked by candidate_ranking.discovery before fanout_top_k is applied. Only valid in hybrid plan_mode.

fanout_top_k.description: How many preliminarily ranked candidates receive this explanation query. This value is explicit and is not the final candidate result limit. When explanations annotate or rerank candidates, it MUST be at least candidate_ranking.discovery.top_k so every preliminary candidate receives the requested explanation before annotation or fair reranking.

ExplanationPostFilter.description: Filters applied to returned paths from the two-endpoint tool. All filters are conjunctive unless stated.

predicate_whitelist.description: Only keep paths where every edge's predicate is one of these active, non-deprecated predicates (or a descendant via Biolink is_a).

predicate_blacklist.description: Drop paths where any edge's predicate is one of these active, non-deprecated predicates (or a descendant).

required_predicates_anywhere.description: Only keep paths where at least one edge uses each of these active, non-deprecated predicates.

required_qualifier_on_any_edge.description: Only keep paths where at least one edge carries all of these qualifier values.

forbidden_qualifier_on_any_edge.description: Drop paths where any edge carries all of these qualifier values.

unique_intermediate_nodes.description: Drop paths that revisit the same node (loops).

top_k_paths.description: Cap on returned paths after post-filter.

group_by_intermediate_category.description: If true, return a diverse set of paths covering different intermediate categories (e.g., one via Gene, one via Pathway) rather than k near-duplicates.

Qualifiers.description: Subset of Biolink qualifier slots most relevant to repurposing. On a Hop, this object is permitted only when the base predicate is biolink:regulates, biolink:affects, or biolink:interacts_with, or an active descendant of one of those families in the loaded model; semantic validation rejects every other predicate–qualifier combination.

qualified_predicate.description: Active, non-deprecated Biolink predicate checked against the loaded model.

origin.description: Whether this ranking preference was explicitly requested by the user or recommended by the planner.

application.description: Ranking criteria are soft preferences and never hard filters.

scope.description: portable criteria use returned Biolink/result fields and can be applied outside the project Executor; executor_specific criteria require the named implementation profile.

profile_id.description: Required for an executor_specific derived criterion; for example, executor_epc_v1 for edge_evidence_strength.

preferred_values.description: Optional ordered values, most preferred first, for categorical criteria such as knowledge_level.

rationale.description: Plain-language explanation usable by a non-Biolink expert.

RankingSpec.description: One explicit ranking stage. Its enclosing field identifies what is ranked: candidate_ranking.discovery, candidate_ranking.final, or explanation_ranking.

criteria.description: Ordered ranking features for this stage.

top_k.description: Result limit for this ranking stage. In candidate_ranking.discovery it is the final candidate limit unless explanation_influence is rerank; in candidate_ranking.final it is the final candidate limit; in explanation_ranking it limits paths after combining explanation-query outputs.

CandidateRanking.description: How discovered candidate entities are ordered. `discovery` is always applied before any candidate-specific explanation fan-out. `final` exists only when explanations are explicitly allowed to rerank candidates.

explanation_influence.description: `none`: explanations are independent context and do not annotate or reorder candidates. `annotate_only`: attach candidate-specific explanations after discovery ranking without changing candidate order. `rerank`: use a preliminary discovery ranking, run candidate-specific explanations, then apply `final` ranking.

rationale.description: Plain-language explanation of why the user's wording calls for this relationship between discovery and explanation ranking.

RankingPlan.description: Stage-specific ranking contract. Discovery plans use candidate_ranking; explanation plans use explanation_ranking; hybrid plans use both.

EvidenceRecommendation.description: A non-filtering recommendation to report evidence metadata alongside results so a human can assess provenance or evidence type.

preferred_values.description: Optional ordered values, most preferred first, when the recommendation is categorical.

EvidencePolicy.description: Hard evidence filters. This object is valid only for filters explicitly requested by the user; planner defaults and recommendations must not be encoded here.

require_primary_knowledge_source.description: Require returned edges to identify the upstream knowledge source that originally asserted the edge. This does not mean primary literature.

attach_explanations_to_candidates.description: In hybrid mode, set true only when from_discovery explanation-query results should be attached to discovery candidates in the final output. Fixed-endpoint fallback queries do not count as candidate explanations.

message.description: Human-facing message. When reason is `needs_clarification`, this SHOULD contain the specific question(s) the planner would ask if it could. No follow-up interaction will occur; the message is informational only.
